title: Tokenization slow-path forensics and dashboard (compact runbook)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact forensic playbook and dashboard recipe for investigating slow-paths introduced by tokenizer behavior and tokenization-related micro-latencies in the inference stack. Intended for on-call, SREs, and serving-runtime engineers who need a fast hypothesis-driven triage flow and a pared-down dashboard to catch intermittent tokenizer-driven spikes without costing a ton of query budget.

Why this doc exists (notes to self):
- We frequently surface 'latency spikes' that collapse to tokenization or pre-processing variability (rare long strings, emoji-heavy inputs, unusual unicode normalization).
- Full trace capture for every request is expensive; need a low-cost signal set + trace anchors for when to escalate to sampling.
- Goal: detect tokenizer slow-paths in <2 min, attribute to component (client, gateway, tokenizer, runtime preproc, tokenizer model shard), and produce minimal trace to repro.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) Instrument three compact metrics (tokenize_p50_ms, tokenize_p99_ms, tokenize_failure_rate).
2) Add token-size histograms and a small session-affinity label (tenant_id, route, model_variant).
3) Build a 6-panel microdash (explained below) and an alert rule: tokenize_p99_ms > 100ms for 5m (with tenant weight).
4) When alert fires, auto-sample traces for requests with token_count > 512 OR contains_non_ascii=true.

Core metrics (definitions):
- tokenize_latency_ms_p50: string. Unit: ms. How: measure wall-clock time inside gateway preprocessing from tokenizer.start to tokenizer.end. Aggregation: p50 per min. Notes: include only successful tokenization attempts (status=ok).
- tokenize_latency_ms_p99: string. Unit: ms. How: same as above, p99 per 1m. Rationale: tokenize slow-paths are heavy-tailed.
- tokenize_token_count_histogram: list of strings. Unit: buckets (0-32,33-64,65-128,129-256,257-512,513-2048). How: record token count emitted by tokenizer per request. Use coarse buckets to keep dimension low.
- tokenizer_unicode_flag: string. Unit: boolean tag (true/false stored as string). How: true if input string contains codepoints outside Basic Latin or contains multi-codepoint grapheme clusters (emoji).
- tokenizer_retries_count: string. Unit: count. How: number of tokenizer internal retries/fallbacks on normalization. Use to detect pathological inputs that trigger iterative normalization loops.
- tokenizer_kv_prefill_hit: string. Unit: boolean tag. How: true if a cached tokenization result for a prompt prefix was used (useful to see cache benefits).

Span and trace design (lightweight anchoring):
- Span hierarchy minimal: request -> gateway-preproc (includes tokenizer) -> runtime-call.
- Add a span annotation key: tokenizer.detail = (fast|slow|error|nonascii) as lightweight string. The value is computed in-process and set before span end.
- Sampling policy: default trace sampling stays low (0.1%); on-detect rule (tokenize_p99_ms > threshold OR tokenizer_retries_count > 0) increase sampling multiplier for 10m for requests where token_count bucket >= 257.
- Trace payload: do NOT include full user prompt in trace; instead include prompt fingerprint (sha256 truncated) and a sanitized token excerpt (first 64 codepoints) with redaction.

Investigation flow (step-by-step):
1) Observe microdash panel: if tokenization p99 spikes but runtime p50 stable => likely tokenizer or gateway preproc.
2) Check token_count histograms: a heavy shift to >512 bucket strongly indicates long input.
3) Look at tokenizer_unicode_flag: high fraction true means unicode/emoji heavy incoming traffic.
4) If tokenization_retries_count > 0: capture a sampled trace and create a repro unit test with the prompt fingerprint.
5) If kv_prefill_hit is low for heavy traffic bursts: consider cache warming strategies or prefix caching tuning.
6) If tokenizer.detail == slow across multiple tenants: route traffic to staging tokenizer shard (if available) and coordinate with infra to isolate hardware/gen issues.
7) Document action and put remediation as follow-up (e.g., add input size limits, better normalization heuristics, or a fast path for ascii-only tokenizer).

Microdash panels (6 compact panels, low-cardinality):
1) Tokenize latency p50/p95/p99 (time-series, stacked). Filter by tenant and route.
2) Token count distribution (stacked histogram by bucket).
3) Fraction non-ascii (tokenizer_unicode_flag true rate) and average token_count for those requests.
4) Tokenizer retries (count) + list of top-5 prompt fingerprints causing retries (as table, link to internal repro page).
5) Runtime latency over same window (p50/p95) — to quickly check if slowdown is before or after runtime.
6) Recent sampled traces (links) with tokenizer.detail tag; show reason code and sanitized excerpt.

Alerting guidance (practical):
- Alert A (tenant-sensitive): tokenize_latency_ms_p99 > 100ms for 5m AND tenant_traffic_share > 0.5% -> P1 to oncall-eng. Use tenant weight to avoid noisy single-tenant alerts.
- Alert B (cost-aware): sustained token_count > 512 with kv_prefill_hit < 10% for 15m -> Page product infra (cost ops) with playbook to enable warm pools.
- Alert C (normalization errors): tokenizer_retries_count > 0 on more than 10 distinct prompt fingerprints in 1h -> create a ticket and flip sampling to 100% for affected fingerprints.

Low-cost trace capture policy (how to keep costs down):
- Make tokenizer detail and token_count available as metrics/labels to avoid broad trace captures.
- Only escalate to 1% trace sampling for requests matching composite rule (p99 spike AND token_count bucket >= 257).
- Persist only truncated sanitized prompt excerpts in traces. Avoid storing full user content. Ensure PHI/PII redaction steps are applied.

Dashboard UX notes (operator-friendly):
- Default view: last 60 minutes, with quick toggles for 'only non-ascii' and 'only token_count>512'.
- Hover tooltip: show exact sample counts and sampling fraction so operator knows confidence.
- Drilldown button: 'Open quick trace sample' that attaches a sanitized sample to JIRA ticket template.
- Compact annotation layer: allow and display deployment events (rollouts) as vertical rulers to correlate with tokenizer releases.

Remediation playbook snippets (short):
- Fast path: if tokenizer_unicode_flag=false and token_count < 128, run ASCII-fast-tokenize subroutine (micro-optimized C path).
- Throttle path: if token_count > 2048, reject early with 413-like response and provide client-side guidance.
- Cache path: add short-term LRU cache keyed by prompt fingerprint for common prefixes (verify privacy constraints).

Open questions & follow-ups (TODO):
- Should we treat emoji-heavy inputs as their own traffic class for routing? (pro: isolated; con: increases routing complexity)
- How to instrument client libraries to set an input-type hint (e.g., isHtml, isCode) without leaking content?
- Evaluate tokenizer normalization heuristics across languages: get linguistics SME (Lena) to review our unicode normalization fallback strategy.

Implementation checklist (owner Priya unless noted):
- [ ] Add metrics: tokenize_latency_ms_(p50,p95,p99), token_count_histogram, tokenizer_unicode_flag (Ethan)
- [ ] Add span annotation tokenizer.detail and sampling rule integration (Ethan)
- [ ] Create microdash panels and alert rules (Priya)
- [ ] Implement ASCII-fast-tokenize toggle behind feature flag (serving-runtime team)
- [ ] Add automatic trace-sample-on-rare-fingerprint and repro page (Lena)
- [ ] Run a 2-week experiment; measure false positives and tracing cost delta (all)

Appendix: quick query snippets (examples):
- token_count bucket query pseudo-SQL: SELECT bucket, count(*) FROM metrics WHERE time > now() - 1h GROUP BY bucket
- p99 join example: SELECT tenant, quantile(0.99)(tokenize_latency_ms) FROM metrics WHERE time > now() - 10m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY p99 DESC LIMIT 20

Redaction/privacy note: do not store full user prompts. Always store fingerprint and at most sanitized excerpt (first 64 codepoints). Any data retention for traces must follow compliance retention settings (see linked_artifacts CONFLUENCE-OBS-2456).

Contact and escalation:
- First responder: Priya Nair (eng-observability). Secondary: Ethan Zhao (serving-runtime). For infra/hardware escalations contact infra-oncall.

Document history:
- 2025-11-02 initial draft
- 2026-01-15 added low-cost trace policy and alert tuning
- 2026-02-28 updated sampling thresholds and added TODOs

Notes to self: this doc should remain small and operator-focused — if it grows into a full investigation guide (long reproduction recipes), split into a separate forensic notebook repo.
